- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high (0.80+) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.75.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral (0.27–0.53) and price is consolidating; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent 3-day mean is flat.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if 10-day moving average is above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to overreact to minor price drops; apply smoothing filter to avoid sharp downward revisions.
